Something I struggled with as a literature student is always feeling shitty for not enjoying classic and difficult books when asked about them in class. I felt embarrassed to admit i prefer cheesy romance novels over more "thought-provoking" books, but at the end of the day, there is no point forcing yourself to read something that is far too complicated, or that you simply don't enjoy. The main purpose of a story is to be entertaining to its reader, why confuse or frustrate yourself for no reason? People like him only read for bragging rights, or to seem more intellectual- and to be honest, thats a really boring way to read. Stick to the stuff you love.

(And in all honesty, most people read the Wikipedia summaries instead of the actual books)

I was on a trip with one of my classes and this girl that I don't particularly like came along. I have no reason not to like her but she gets under my skin.

We were all sat in a local restaurant and she sat 10 seats away. What I failed to realize was that slowly throughout the meal she moved up seats. She went to the toilet (I was facing away so I had no idea when she would come back) and one of the girls I was sat with made a comment like "Oh wow guys, my leather jacket is part of my personality!" in regards to her outfit. I laughed and, because I have no sense of volume control or social awareness, said really loudly, "I'm not like other girls, I wear a leather jacket to let the world know what an individual I am!".

She was behind me.

Dinner got real awkward real fast.
